blocks.text: Public policy is 'whatever governments choose to do or not to do' (**Thomas Dye**). The **policy cycle**: agenda-setting → formulation → legitimation → **implementation** → evaluation → feedback. Indian policy instruments span **laws** (rights-based: RTI, NREGA, RTE, NFSA), **schemes** (centrally sponsored & central sector), **missions** (mission-mode: Swachh Bharat, Jal Jeevan), **regulation** (SEBI, RBI, TRAI) and **transfers** (DBT on the JAM trinity — Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile).

rows: **Ayushman Bharat** — PM-JAY (₹5 lakh cover) + Health & Wellness Centres; **National Health Mission**
**PM Gati Shakti**, Bharatmala/Sagarmala, **PMAY (U&G)**, Jal Jeevan Mission (har ghar jal)
Public digital infrastructure (DPI) as policy platform
**PLI schemes**, Make in India, MSP + PM-AASHA, e-NAM, FPOs
PM-JANMAN, Stand-Up India, **PM Vishwakarma**, NSAP pensions

sections.heading: The AP policy stack — must-cite specifics

items: **Direct-transfer welfare architecture**: AP pioneered saturation DBT — farmer investment support (**Rythu Bharosa**, topping up PM-KISAN), education incentives (**Amma Vodi / Talliki Vandanam** era schemes), fee reimbursement — study them as the *saturation + DBT + secretariat-delivery* model.
**Delivery innovation**: village/ward **secretariats (2019)** and volunteers; **Spandana** grievance platform; e-crop booking for farm subsidies — administrative capillaries most states lack.

**Sectoral pushes**: AP Industrial Development Policy, port-led growth (Sagarmala alignment, new ports at Ramayapatnam, Machilipatnam, Bhavanapadu), renewable-energy parks, natural farming (**APCNF** — internationally cited community-managed natural farming).
Evaluation lens: high welfare coverage vs **fiscal stress** (debt/GSDP among the higher states), capex squeeze, and dependency debates — a balanced mains evaluation must carry both sides.

sections.heading: How to evaluate any intervention (the reusable grid)

items: **Design**: universal vs targeted? rights-based vs discretionary? conditionality? — e.g., NFSA's legal right vs scheme-based discretion.
**Coverage & targeting errors**: inclusion/exclusion errors (PDS studies), SECC vs income-certificate targeting.
**Delivery**: leakage before/after DBT (**DBT savings claims ~₹3.5 lakh crore cumulative**), last-mile authentication failures.
**Outcomes vs outputs**: toilets built vs open-defecation behaviour; enrolment vs learning (**ASER** gaps).
**Fiscal sustainability & incentives**: subsidy vs capex balance; freebies debate (**RBI State Finances reports**).
**Federal fit**: one-size CSS vs state flexibility (Sub-group of CMs on CSS recommended 60:40 sharing & flexi-funds).

blocks.text: Exam tip: Never list schemes — evaluate two per sector using the grid (design → targeting → delivery → outcome → fiscal). Pair one central and one AP scheme in every answer; APPSC examiners specifically reward the AP pairing.

blocks.text: **The modern turn:** **evidence-based policy** and **behavioural 'nudge'** design (India's own thinking reflected in Economic Survey chapters), **randomised evaluation** (the 2019 Nobel to Banerjee-Duflo-Kremer), and **outcome budgeting**. Cite **DBT/JAM (Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile)** as India's flagship in plugging leakages, and **NITI Aayog's SDG India Index & Aspirational Districts Programme** as data-driven policy steering.

prelimsPointers: **Incrementalism / 'muddling through'** — Charles Lindblom; **Mixed scanning** — Amitai Etzioni.
**JAM trinity** (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile) underpins **Direct Benefit Transfer**.
**MGNREGA**: legal guarantee of **100 days** per rural household; wages linked to CPI-AL; social audit statutorily mandated (Sec 17).
**NFSA 2013** covers **75% rural / 50% urban** population; 5 kg per person per month; Antyodaya 35 kg per household.
**PM-JAY**: ₹5 lakh per family per year, ~55 crore beneficiaries targeted; AP's counterpart heritage is **Aarogyasri (2007)** — the model for national health insurance.
**JAM trinity** enabling **DBT** — started with LPG (**PAHAL**), among the world's largest cash-transfer rails.
**PM Gati Shakti (2021)**: national master plan for multimodal infrastructure on a GIS platform.
**APCNF** (community-managed natural farming) is AP's globally cited agro-ecology programme.
CSS sharing pattern for most schemes: **60:40** (90:10 for NE/Himalayan states) after the 14th FC.
mainsAngles: Rights-based legislation transformed Indian welfare from patronage to entitlement — discuss with MGNREGA, RTI, RTE and NFSA.
Digital public infrastructure is India's distinctive policy innovation — examine how JAM-DBT changed welfare delivery, with AP's secretariat model as a case.
Evaluate the saturation-welfare model of Andhra Pradesh on coverage, outcomes and fiscal sustainability.
Centrally sponsored schemes homogenise what federalism should differentiate — critically examine with reform suggestions.
Outputs are counted, outcomes are assumed — critique India's scheme-evaluation culture with examples.

glossary.definition: Scheme funded jointly by Centre and states (typically 60:40) and implemented by states in State/Concurrent List areas — the main instrument of central influence on state priorities.
Transfer of scheme benefits straight to Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts, minimising intermediaries and leakage; built on the JAM trinity.
Delivering a benefit to every eligible person rather than phased targeting — reduces exclusion error and discretion; fiscally demanding.
Targeting failures: benefits reaching the non-poor (inclusion) or missing the eligible poor (exclusion) — the core diagnostic of welfare design.
Time-bound, outcome-focused implementation vehicle with dedicated governance (e.g., Swachh Bharat, Jal Jeevan) as against routine departmental delivery.

sections.heading: Implementation — where policy goes to struggle

blocks.text: Implementation is the **conversion of policy intent into outcomes** through organisations, money, people and processes. **Pressman & Wildavsky** (*Implementation*, 1973) showed how the 'complexity of joint action' — many actors, many clearances — defeats even well-designed programmes. India's classic gap: **excellent policy, uneven delivery** — what the Economic Survey once called the difference between *outlays and outcomes*.

rows: Over-ambition, one-size-fits-all CSS, unclear objectives, poor piloting
Farm laws' consultation deficit; frequent scheme renaming/overlap
Vacancies, generalist churn (short tenures), weak state capability at the last mile
District-level vacancies; average collector tenure < 2 years in many states
Delayed fund release, parked funds, unspent balances, treasury single-account issues
MGNREGA wage-payment delays; SNA reforms (2021) to track CSS floats
Sanitation = water + health + education + behaviour; Gati Shakti created precisely to break silos
Target-chasing, data gaming, weak M&E, no consequence for failure
Leakage, elite capture of benefits, contractor nexus

items: **Delivery-unit approach**: PRAGATI (PM's tech-enabled review), project-monitoring groups, CM dashboards (AP's real-time governance heritage) — escalation with named accountability.
**Process re-engineering before digitisation**: DBT, e-FMS, JIT fund release (SNA/TSA), faceless & paperless interfaces — 'digitise the reformed process, not the broken one'.
**Convergence & saturation**: Aspirational Districts Programme (rank–support–compete on 49 indicators), mission convergence at district level.
**People**: tenure stability (SC in **T.S.R. Subramanian, 2013** — fixed tenures, civil services boards), specialist lateral entry, iGOT-Karmayogi capability building.

**Accountability from below**: social audit (MGNREGA Sec 17; **Meghalaya's social-audit law**), citizen charters with penalties (**AP Public Services Delivery Guarantee framework**), Spandana-style grievance redress with timelines.
**Evaluate and sunset**: NITI's DMEO, outcome budgets, third-party evaluation; close what fails.

sections.heading: The AP implementation story — both sides

items: **Strengths**: secretariat-volunteer capillaries deliver DBT with low friction; **Spandana** institutionalised grievance timelines; e-crop and land-records digitisation cut discretion; Aarogyasri's empanelment model showed process innovation at scale.

**Weaknesses to cite fairly**: scheme continuity ruptures with political cycles (renamed/paused schemes), capex crowd-out by committed welfare expenditure, contractor-payment arrears affecting works programmes, and Polavaram's time/cost overruns as the emblematic mega-project implementation case.

Use **Polavaram** as your full-spectrum example: inter-state clearances, R&R (rehabilitation of displaced tribal families), funding-pattern disputes with the Centre, technical redesign (diaphragm wall damage), and repeated deadline slippage — every implementation pathology in one project.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Name the seven problem clusters, then give fix-for-problem pairs (vacancy→tenure reform; leakage→DBT+social audit; silo→convergence). End with Polavaram or MGNREGA as a threaded case study. Pressman & Wildavsky + 'outlay vs outcome' phrasing signal conceptual command.

sections.heading: 🏛 Deep mastery — the implementation gap, diagnosed

items: **Classic diagnosis:** *Pressman & Wildavsky* ('**Implementation**', 1973) showed how each additional clearance point multiplies the odds of failure — the 'complexity of joint action'.

**Top-down vs bottom-up:** top-down (Sabatier-Mazmanian) stresses clear goals and control; bottom-up (Lipsky's **'street-level bureaucrats'**) shows frontline discretion actually shapes policy — the ASHA, the anganwadi worker, the VRO ARE the policy to the citizen.

**Indian failure modes:** the **'implementation deficit'** — leakages (the old '15 paise of a rupee reaches' critique attributed to Rajiv Gandhi), elite capture, weak monitoring, and fund-flow delays.

**What fixes it:** DBT, geo-tagging & MIS (e.g., MGNREGA's NREGASoft), social audit, **outcome monitoring**, decentralised delivery, and technology-enabled last-mile grids like **AP's Village/Ward Secretariats + Volunteers**.

prelimsPointers: *Implementation* (1973) — **Pressman & Wildavsky**; 'complexity of joint action'.
**Street-level bureaucrats** — Michael Lipsky's concept of frontline discretion.
mainsAngles: 'Policies fail not in design but in delivery' — examine the implementation gap in Indian welfare programmes with remedies.

prelimsPointers: **Pressman & Wildavsky (1973)** — founding study of implementation; 'complexity of joint action'.
**PRAGATI** (2015): PM's ICT-based multi-modal platform for Pro-Active Governance And Timely Implementation.
**Aspirational Districts Programme (2018)**: NITI Aayog; 112 districts; 5 themes, 49 indicators; AP districts included.
**SNA (Single Nodal Agency) system, 2021** tracks CSS funds to curb parked balances.
**T.S.R. Subramanian v. Union (2013)**: SC directed fixed tenures and Civil Services Boards for postings/transfers.
MGNREGA **Section 17** statutorily mandates **social audit** of works.
**DMEO** (Development Monitoring & Evaluation Office) under NITI Aayog conducts scheme evaluations.
mainsAngles: 'India does not have a policy problem; it has an implementation problem' — critically examine with sectoral evidence.
Identify the administrative, fiscal and informational bottlenecks in scheme implementation and match each with a proven reform.
Mega-project implementation in India is a study in the complexity of joint action — analyse using the Polavaram project.
Social audit and grievance-redress systems shift accountability from process to outcome — evaluate with MGNREGA and AP's Spandana.
Frequent transfers are the unpriced tax on Indian administration — discuss tenure-security reforms after T.S.R. Subramanian.

glossary.definition: The distance between policy objectives and realised outcomes, produced by design, capacity, funding, coordination and incentive failures.
Pressman & Wildavsky's phrase for how multiplying actors and decision points geometrically reduces the probability of successful implementation.
Budget documents mapping outlays to measurable outputs and outcomes per scheme — shifting review from spending to results.
Verification of records against ground reality by the beneficiary community itself (Gram Sabha), statutorily required under MGNREGA.
The final administrative link where services meet citizens — the stage where authentication, staffing and access failures concentrate.
Aligning multiple schemes/departments on a shared geography or outcome (e.g., Aspirational Districts) to overcome silo implementation.

sections.heading: The development mosaic beyond the state

blocks.text: Development is co-produced. **Civil society** — 'the arena, outside family, state and market, where people associate to advance common interests' — includes **NGOs/VOs, SHGs, cooperatives, trade unions, faith-based bodies, media, academia and community-based organisations (CBOs)**. Constitutional soil: **Art 19(1)(c)** (association), **Art 43** (cooperatives in DPSP), **Part IXB** (97th Amendment — cooperatives), and the deep Gandhian lineage of **constructive work** (Sarvodaya, Bhoodan).

rows: Service delivery, innovation pilots, rights advocacy, watchdog
**MKSS** → RTI movement; Pratham (ASER); SEWA; Akshaya Patra (mid-day meals)
**AP is the SHG heartland** — DWCRA→Velugu/**SERP**→NRLM's national template; bank-linkage model born in undivided AP
World Bank, UN agencies, Global Fund/GAVI

sections.heading: Contributions, tensions and the regulatory tightrope

items: **Contributions**: last-mile reach where the state is thin; voice for the voiceless (PILs by CSOs — Vishaka arose from an NGO coalition); policy authorship (**RTI from MKSS's jan sunwais; MGNREGA, FRA, NFSA from campaign coalitions**); innovation the state later scales (SHG bank linkage, ASHA-type community workers).
**Tensions**: accountability of the unelected; foreign-funding politics; briefcase NGOs; advocacy vs 'anti-development' labelling of protest (dam/mining/nuclear cases).

**Regulatory frame**: registration (Societies Act 1860/Trusts/Sec-8 companies), **FCRA 2010 (tightened 2020** — Aadhaar of office-bearers, SBI Delhi account, 20% admin cap, no sub-granting), CSR rules, **NITI Darpan** portal, income-tax 12A/80G. SC in **Noel Harper (2022)** upheld the FCRA amendments; critics note FCRA licence numbers have fallen sharply — the 'shrinking civic space' debate.

**Way forward (2nd ARC, 'Social Capital' report)**: accreditation instead of suspicion, transparent grant regimes, outcome-based partnership contracts, protect advocacy as democratic function while auditing funds strictly.

sections.heading: The AP story — civil society as state partner

items: **SERP (Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty)** and the **Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham** SHG movement made undivided AP the national laboratory of women's federations (village → mandal → zilla samakhyas) — the direct ancestor of **NRLM (2011)**; cite **~9 lakh SHGs / crore-scale membership in AP** as the density fact.
**APCNF (natural farming)** runs through farmer federations and CRPs (community resource persons) — a civil-society-method programme inside government.
**Watchdog lineage**: social audits of NREGA were pioneered in undivided AP (SSAAT — the first state social-audit society), later a national model.
Balanced note: partnership can shade into **co-option** — SHG federations mobilised for state schemes raise the autonomy question; a strong mains conclusion holds both partnership and independence.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Anchor with the 2nd ARC 'Social Capital' report, one law (FCRA 2020 + Noel Harper 2022), one movement-to-law chain (MKSS→RTI), and the AP SHG/SSAAT story. The examiner wants roles + tensions + regulation + way forward, not an NGO catalogue.

sections.heading: 🏛 Deep mastery — the state, market and civil society triangle

items: **Beyond government to governance:** development is co-produced by the **state, market (CSR under Section 135, Companies Act 2013), civil society/NGOs, and communities (SHGs, cooperatives)**.

**SHG revolution:** the **DAY-NRLM/SERP** self-help-group movement — AP and undivided AP pioneered it — mobilised crores of rural women into savings-and-credit groups, a globally cited model of social capital and financial inclusion.

**The regulatory tightrope:** the **FCRA (amended 2020)** tightened foreign-funding scrutiny of NGOs, raising the 'accountability vs civil-society space' debate; a balanced answer defends both probity and the associational freedom under Art 19(1)(c).

**PPP & the market:** infrastructure via PPP (VGF, HAM models), and the **Kelkar Committee (2015)** on revitalising PPP, show the market as a development partner — needing strong regulation to protect public interest.

mainsAngles: 'Civil society is the third pillar of development governance' — assess the role and regulation of NGOs in India.

prelimsPointers: **2nd ARC, 9th Report — 'Social Capital: A Shared Destiny'** covers NGOs, SHGs and cooperatives.
**FCRA 2010, amended 2020**: FC funds only in an **SBI New Delhi main branch** account; **sub-granting prohibited**; admin expenses capped at **20%**; upheld in **Noel Harper v. Union (2022)**.
**CSR**: Companies Act 2013, **Sec 135** — 2% of average net profits (3-yr) for companies meeting thresholds; Schedule VII activities.
**97th Amendment (2011)**: cooperatives — Art 19(1)(c) expanded, **Art 43B**, Part IXB (Part IXB partly struck for states in **Rajendra Shah, 2021**, valid for multi-state cooperatives).
**MKSS's** jan sunwai movement (Rajasthan) catalysed **RTI 2005**.
AP's **SERP** (2000) and social-audit society **SSAAT** were national firsts; NRLM scaled the AP SHG model.
**NITI Darpan**: NGO registration portal for government grants.
mainsAngles: Civil society is the third pillar of development, neither state nor market — examine its distinctive contributions with Indian examples.
From MKSS to MGNREGA, India's rights laws were authored on the streets — discuss the policy role of social movements.
Regulation of foreign-funded NGOs balances sovereignty against civic space — critically evaluate the FCRA regime after 2020.
The Andhra SHG movement shows the state scaling civil-society method — analyse its achievements and the co-option risk.
Suggest a partnership framework between government and voluntary organisations based on the 2nd ARC's Social Capital report.

glossary.definition: The associational space between family, state and market where citizens organise for shared purposes — NGOs, SHGs, unions, media, faith bodies, CBOs.
Networks of trust and reciprocity that enable collective action (Putnam); the 2nd ARC's frame for India's NGO-SHG-cooperative sector.
10–20 member savings-and-credit affinity group, bank-linked and federated; the AP-pioneered backbone of NRLM's women's livelihoods architecture.
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 (amended 2020) governing foreign donations to associations — registration, designated SBI account, use restrictions.
Joint delivery of public services by state agencies and citizen groups (e.g., social audits, community health workers), combining authority with local knowledge.
Organisation whose primary work is influencing policy and defending rights rather than delivering services — the segment most affected by regulatory tightening.
